description: We’re building the Earth Information Jukebox: a web app that turns NASA Earth Information Center visualizations into live, music-like soundscapes, so Earth science can be heard, not just seen, and is accessible to blind and low-vision users. Stack: React, TypeScript, Tone.js. Looking for: a sound designer or musician to tune the mappings, an accessibility or Earth-science reviewer, and a designer or video editor for the demo.
summary: Planetary Playlist is an accessible Earth Jukebox that lets people hear ten curated NASA Earth Information Center visualizations. Choose a bundled NASA frame and the playhead sweeps across it while a browser-based sonification engine translates visible color, brightness, contrast, and position into a live, scale-locked soundscape. The experience pairs scientific descriptions and source credits with keyboard controls, screen-reader labels, reduced-motion support, and a visual sound key. It is important because Earth science is often presented only through sight; Planetary Playlist lets blind, low-vision, and sighted audiences explore the same Earth stories through sound without sacrificing scientific context.
details: Each frame is analysed once into a 96 × 32 grid. Salient cells become deterministic note events: row maps to pitch inside an author-selected scale, column maps to time and stereo position, visible hue selects a synth voice, and brightness/salience affect loudness and density. Tone.js schedules the events through a low-pass filter, algorithmic reverb, compressor, limiter, and a conservative root drone. All assets are bundled locally so the demo does not depend on runtime NASA API calls or venue Wi-Fi. The interface is built with Vite, React, TypeScript, plain CSS, Vitest, Playwright, and axe-core.
